newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Oilseeds-Sky-high US prices spark scramble.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Oilseeds-Sky-high US prices spark scramble.

text.p: Steadily rising U.S. soybean prices have fuelled intense competition among Taiwan buyers, with key rivals watching each others' moves by the minute and taking rare interest in non-U.S. supplies.
Following in the steps of some major U.S. soybean buyers, Taiwan buyers were simply turning away from pricey U.S. supplies, traders said.
"Even U.S. buyers have bought some Brazilian soybeans, so what are we waiting for?" a Taiwan buyer said.

At a tender on Wednesday, the Kaohsiung division of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association bought a 54,000-tonne shipment of south American soybeans, specifying they be sourced in Argentina or southern Brazil.

Even before the deal was struck, the arch rival Taichung division announced its own tender for a similar shipment -- but declined to provide complete specifications while it waited to see what kind of terms the Kaohsiung group would get.

The Taichung and Kaohsiung divisions of Taiwan's Breakfast Soybean Procurement Association, Taiwan's main soybean buyers, have both taken what for them is the rare step of sourcing soybeans in south America.
The two groups, which have operated independently for decades despite their similar names, are fiercely competitive with one often arranging tenders on the basis of what price the other gets.
Even in normal times, the two groups normally arrange tenders within few days of each other. That competitive instinct has surged along with the price of U.S. soy futures.
The Kaohsiung division's tender on Wednesday prompted the Taichung division to inform traders to prepare for a tender for a similar 54,000-tonne shipment on Thursday.
But as the Kaohsiung tender dragged on into the late afternoon, the Taichung rivals were unable to make final decisions about their own specifications, traders said.
"Kaohsiung's Wednesday tender result came after 5.30 p.m. (0930 GMT), so Taichung wasn't able to finish its tender details on Wednesday," a trader said.

Traders said Taichung division was likely to move Thursday's announced tender to Friday or even next Tuesday to give suppliers time to prepare, although it could follow through on the Thursday tender by notifying suppliers of the specifications in the morning.
As long as U.S. prices remain high, Taiwan buyers will see south American soybeans as attractive, considering the Latin alternative if prices are US$10 or more per tonne below U.S. soybeans.
The BSPA's Kaohsiung division was preparing to send delegates to Brazil in April to review crop planting, silo facilities and port conditions, traders said.

Taiwan's Hui Shung Group also was known to be waiting for the right moment to buy 38,500 tonnes of soybeans and 16,000 tonnes of corn and was likely to turn to Argentina for the combined shipment, a group buyer has said.
Traders said Hui Shung would likely to buy based on the result of the BSPA Taichung division's tender.
Hui Shung group does not always arrange its tenders close to the two main soybean buying groups, but is expected to do so this time due to the volatile U.S. futures market, they said.
State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp will tender on Friday for a combined shipment of 20,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 10,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans.
